interpretation: Spatial continuity is locally redundant but carried by taxonomically different species across sites. Richer sites contain more individually sufficient species while dominance weakens, without an increasing fraction of eligible species becoming sufficient.

supported_descriptive: continuity-carrier identity turns over strongly among sites
multiple species are individually sufficient at many sites
no single species is a continent-wide continuity carrier
not_supported: the carrier role is a conserved functional trait
taxonomic turnover among sites is itself surprising given geographic separation
